name: Roman Numerals
morphology: Roman numerals are formed by combining seven symbols (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) using additive and subtractive rules.
hierarchy: Symbols increase in magnitude from I (1) to M (1000). Subtractive pairs form special values such as 4 (IV) and 9 (IX).
context: Roman numerals originated in ancient Rome and were used throughout the Roman Empire in trade, architecture, and numbering.
rules: Roman numerals use seven base symbols: I, V, X, L, C, D, M.
Symbols placed after a larger value are additive (VIII = 5 + 3).
Symbols placed before a larger value are subtractive (IV = 4, IX = 9).
Only powers of 10 (I, X, C) may be used subtractively, never V, L, or D.
A numeral may not repeat more than three times in succession (III = 3, but IIII is invalid).
V, L, and D are never repeated.
The subtractive forms are fixed: IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM.
Numbers are read left to right from largest to smallest groups.
